concepts.name: zip for parallel iteration
concepts.description: `zip()` lazily pairs items from iterables in parallel; plain zip stops at the shortest input, while `strict=True` raises `ValueError` on unequal lengths.

concepts.name: Unzipping with *
concepts.description: `zip(*pairs)` expands the rows as positional arguments and groups values by position, a common transpose/unzip idiom.

concepts.name: enumerate with explicit start
concepts.description: `enumerate(iterable, start)` yields index-value pairs; `start` changes the counter's initial value without skipping iterable items.

concepts.name: Nested comprehensions
concepts.description: Multiple `for` clauses in a comprehension follow the same order as equivalent nested loops.

concepts.name: Dictionary comprehensions
concepts.description: A dictionary comprehension builds key-value pairs, supports filtering, requires hashable keys, and keeps the later value when a key repeats.

concepts.name: next() with generator and default
concepts.description: `next(iterator, default)` returns one item or the default on exhaustion; paired with a generator expression it is a lazy first-match idiom.

concepts.name: Calling with *args
concepts.description: A single `*` in a call expands an iterable into positional arguments; the resulting arguments still must fit the callable's signature.

concepts.name: Calling with **kwargs
concepts.description: A double `**` in a call expands a mapping into keyword arguments; keys must be strings and duplicate parameter assignment raises `TypeError`.

concepts.name: Dictionary ** unpacking precedence
concepts.description: Inside a dictionary display, `**mapping` merges entries left to right and later values replace earlier values for duplicate keys.

concepts.name: Compound sort keys
concepts.description: Tuple sort keys compare lexicographically; numeric negation can reverse one field, and stable sorting enables clear multi-pass mixed-direction sorts.

concepts.name: Assignment expressions
concepts.description: `:=` binds and returns a value inside an expression so it can be tested and reused without recomputation.
